mainRoof.notes: Main gable with ridge front-to-back (large gables facing front and rear, wide eaves overhang). A lower cross gable with ridge along the front covers the garage wing on the right and ends in a gable facing right; two valleys where it meets the main roof. Gables have white barge boards and boxed soffits.

largeGlazing.what: two-pane living-room terrace glazing, about 2.9 m wide on the rear elevation, floor to ceiling

features.where: one in the front gable and one in the rear gable (attic level), each a cantilevered slab with glass balustrade on steel posts
3 on the left roof plane of the main roof; 2 side by side on the front plane of the garage-wing roof; 1 on the right plane of the main roof near the front
two white rendered chimneys on the main roof: one on the left plane near the ridge (fireplace), one on the right plane towards the rear; plus small vent pipes at the ridge
one white square column at the entrance recess (front), one at the covered terrace recess (rear)
timber deck along the rear and wrapping to the left side; timber steps at the entrance

palette.walls: white render on the gables / upper part, olive-beige (khaki) render on the ground floor, warm oak-coloured timber window frames, infill panels and garage door
palette.roof: dark graphite flat concrete tiles; white barge boards and soffits

uncertain: FRONT storey 0, left to right: kitchen corner window (two sashes, timber panel at the corner), two small high windows (pantry and bathroom) joined by a timber panel into one visual band - counted as 2 WINDOWs because the plan shows two separate openings in two rooms; entrance door with a narrow glazed sidelight on its left (one opening); a separate tall narrow window of the utility closet to the right of a timber panel; garage door.
FRONT and REAR storey 1: in each gable two separate glazed balcony doors (two rooms) with a timber infill panel between them; they read as one ~2.9 m wide composition but are 2 openings on the plan.

REAR storey 0, seen from outside left to right: two small high utility-room windows joined by a timber panel (counted as 2), two-leaf glazed door of the ground-floor room (~1.7 m) in the covered recess, then the living-room glazing (~2.9 m). The plan additionally shows a single door leaf at the right end of the living-room glazing / on the short return wall facing the covered terrace; it is not separately readable on the rear elevation and is not counted.

LEFT storey 0: the centre opening is a two-leaf floor-to-ceiling glazed unit about 2.3-2.5 m wide (borderline with LARGE_GLAZING); the right one is the kitchen corner window (also counted once on FRONT).

RIGHT storey 0, left (front) to right (rear): two small garage windows joined by a timber panel (counted as 2), a solid timber side door to the utility room near the rear end. RIGHT storey 1: one two-sash window in the garage-wing gable (storage attic).
The kitchen window is a corner window: one part faces FRONT, one part faces LEFT; each is counted on its own facade.
Garage-wing and main-body sizes are scaled from the plan using the printed 1292 x 1172 cm outline; treat as +/- 0.3 m.
confidence: HIGH - four elevation drawings, both floor plans, a dimensioned roof plan and renders are mutually consistent; remaining doubt is only how to count paired small windows joined by timber panels.
